subject: Weekly Revision
summary: all five topics of Week 1: statics, trusses and friction; kinematics and dynamics; linear algebra; impulse, energy and impact; stress, strain and Mohr's circle (3 questions each)

questions.text: A 1000 N block is to be pulled up a rough plane inclined at 20° (μ = 0.25) by a force P inclined at θ to the plane, as shown. The least value of P that can just start the block up the plane is
solution: Concept: P is least when it is inclined to the plane at the angle of friction φ = tan⁻¹μ; then Pmin = W sin(α + φ).
Check: P parallel to the plane needs W(sin α + μ cos α) = 576.9 N, which is larger. ✔
Exam tip: "Least force" problems: tilt the force by φ. For a horizontal floor the answer reduces to Pmin = W sin φ.

questions.text: The beam ABC shown is supported by a pin at A and a roller at B. It carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over AB and a point load of 30 kN at the free end C. The reaction at A (in kN, upward) is ______
solution: Concept: Take moments about the other support to get one reaction directly.
Moments about B (clockwise +): R<sub>A</sub>(6) − 60(3) + 30(2) = 0
Exam tip: A load on the overhang relieves the far support: here it reduces RA from 30 kN to 20 kN. (Useful for Day 7: SFD & BMD.)

questions.text: Block A (100 N) rests on block B (200 N), which rests on the floor. A is tied to the wall by a horizontal string, as shown. μ = 0.3 at both contact surfaces. The horizontal force P needed to just move B is
solution: Concept: Draw the FBD of B: it is resisted by friction from A on its top face and from the floor on its bottom face.
Top face: F₁ = μN₁ = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N (A is held by the string)
Exam tip: If A were free (no string), the blocks would move together and P = 90 N only.

questions.text: A ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m/s from the top of a 45 m high cliff. Its speed just before hitting the level ground below (in m/s) is ______ (g = 9.81 m/s²)
solution: Concept: Horizontal velocity stays constant; vertical velocity grows as in free fall.
v = √(20² + 882.9) = 35.82 m/s, at 56.1° below the horizontal
Exam tip: Energy gives it in one line: v² = u² + 2gh.

questions.text: Rain falls vertically at 12 m/s. A man walks on level ground at 5 m/s. To protect himself best, he should hold his umbrella tilted
solution: Concept: The umbrella must face the velocity of rain relative to the man: vrain/man = vrain − vman.
Relative velocity: 12 m/s down and 5 m/s backwards; magnitude 13 m/s
Angle with the vertical: tan⁻¹(5/12) = 22.6°, so rain appears to come from the front → tilt the umbrella forward.
Exam tip: tan⁻¹(12/5) = 67.4° is the angle with the horizontal, a common trap.

questions.text: A 10 kg mass hangs from a light rope wound round a drum of radius 0.25 m, which turns on a frictionless fixed axle (moment of inertia of the drum I = 0.5 kg·m²), as shown. The acceleration of the mass when released (in m/s²) is ______ (g = 9.81 m/s²)
solution: Concept: Mass: mg − T = ma. Drum: Tr = Iα with a = αr.
Exam tip: The drum adds an "equivalent mass" I/r² (= 8 kg here) in the denominator: a = mg/(m + I/r²).

questions.text:
The matrix
123
24k
369
has rank 1 when
solution: Concept: Rank 1 means every row is a multiple of the first row.
R₃ = 3R₁ already. R₂ = 2R₁ needs k = 2 × 3 = 6.
For any other k, rows 1 and 2 are independent and the rank is 2 (it can never be 3, since R₃ = 3R₁).
Exam tip: For rank questions, look for proportional rows before expanding determinants.

questions.text:
For A =
31
13
, the value of det(A³) is ______
solution: Concept: det(An) = (det A)n; also det A = product of eigenvalues.
det A = 9 − 1 = 8 (eigenvalues 4 and 2: 4 × 2 = 8 ✔)
Exam tip: Never multiply the matrix out: work with the determinant or eigenvalues (here 64 × 8 = 512).

questions.text: If Q is a real orthogonal matrix, which of the following is NOT necessarily true?
opts: All eigenvalues of Q are real
questions.ans: (C) All eigenvalues of Q are real
solution: Concept: Orthogonal: QᵀQ = I.
So Q⁻¹ = Qᵀ, det Q = ±1, and all eigenvalues have modulus 1.
But the eigenvalues need not be real: the 2-D rotation matrix [cos θ, −sin θ; sin θ, cos θ] has eigenvalues e±iθ. Hence (C) is not necessarily true.
Exam tip: Symmetric → real eigenvalues; orthogonal → |λ| = 1; skew-symmetric → zero or purely imaginary.

questions.text: A car moving at 72 km/h on a level road is braked to rest with all wheels locked. If μ = 0.6 between the tyres and the road, the stopping distance (in m) is ______ (g = 9.81 m/s²)
solution: Concept: Work–energy: friction work = loss of KE; the mass cancels.
u = 72 km/h = 20 m/s
Exam tip: Stopping distance ∝ u²: doubling the speed makes it four times longer.

questions.text: A 3 kg ball moving at 4 m/s makes a direct central impact with a 1 kg ball at rest. If e = 0.8, the velocities of the 3 kg and 1 kg balls after impact are
solution: Concept: Momentum + Newton's law of restitution.
Check: e = 1 gives 2 and 6 m/s; e = 0 gives 3 and 3 m/s.
Exam tip: General results: v₁ = (m₁ − em₂)u₁/(m₁ + m₂), v₂ = (1 + e)m₁u₁/(m₁ + m₂).

questions.text: A lift of total mass 800 kg is raised at a steady 1.5 m/s. If the efficiency of the drive is 80 %, the input power needed (in kW) is ______ (g = 9.81 m/s²)
solution: Concept: At constant speed, the pull equals the weight; power = force × velocity.
Exam tip: Divide by efficiency for input; multiplying (9.42 kW) is the common slip.

questions.text: For an isotropic material whose bulk modulus K is equal to its Young's modulus E, Poisson's ratio is
solution: Concept: E = 3K(1 − 2ν).
Exam tip: Remember the landmarks: ν = 1/3 → K = E; ν = 0.5 → K = ∞; ν = 0 → K = E/3.

questions.text: At a point, σx = 40 MPa (tensile), σy = 60 MPa (compressive) and τxy = 40 MPa. The major principal stress (in MPa) is ______
solution: Concept: σ1 = C + R from Mohr's circle.
Exam tip: Keep signs: σy = −60, so (σx − σy)/2 = 50, not −10.

questions.text: A prismatic bar is fixed between two rigid supports and heated uniformly. The thermal stress developed in it is independent of
solution: Concept: σ = Eα ΔT for full restraint.
The strain prevented is αΔT (a strain, not a length), so the stress depends on E, α and ΔT only.
It is independent of the length (and of the cross-sectional area). The force, σA, does depend on the area.
Exam tip: Length matters only when there is a gap or a yielding support: then strain = (αΔT L − gap)/L.
